A consumer-to-consumer (C2C) sale between two private persons
e: Platforms targeting the Philippine market are covered.
C2C transactions and online media content are excluded.

s: Which agency administers the Internet Transactions Act?
o: Department of Information and Communications Technology
e: The Act covers B2B and B2C internet transactions under DTI.
That is not the agency named.

s: Under RA 11765, a "financial consumer" is a person who:
o: Owns a bank or lending company
Buys, leases or receives, or may do so, financial products from a provider
Works as a teller in a bank
e: That is a provider, not a consumer.
Sec. 3 defines financial consumers this way, including prospective ones.
The definition covers financial service providers.
An employee is not the definition.

s: A family's income is ₱30,000 a month. Under the 50-30-20 guide, how much goes to savings and debt payments?
e: That is 50%, the share for needs.
That is 30%, the share for wants.

s: Which of the following is a FIXED expense?
o: Electricity used for an air conditioner in summer
e: Fixed expenses such as rent do not change over time.

s: A family pays ₱6,000 for insurance once a year. How should it appear in the monthly budget?
o: It should be left out of the budget
₱6,000 in one month and nothing after
e: Divide the bill by the number of months it covers: 6,000 ÷ 12 = 500.
The source says spread it monthly.

s: In budgeting, what should a family do if total monthly expenses are higher than income?
o: Ignore it until the end of the year
Borrow every month to cover the gap
Adjust the budget after comparing income and expenses
e: The source says to adjust the budget.
The budget steps say total, compare, and adjust if expenses are higher.

s: Simple interest is computed on the:
o: Price of the item bought with the loan only
Principal, using the annual rate and the term in years
Interest already earned in earlier years
e: Income is not part of the formula.
The principal is the amount borrowed or deposited.
Simple interest uses the principal, rate and time.

s: ₱10,000 is deposited at 5% simple interest per year for 3 years. How much interest is earned?
e: That is one year's interest only.
That is roughly compound interest, not simple.

s: Which of the following is a unit of competency in TESDA Housekeeping NC II?
o: Clean and prepare rooms for incoming guests
Install electrical wiring in a residential building
Draft and cut patterns for casual apparel
Prepare hot and cold sauces for the menu
e: This is one of the listed core units.

s: Under the Consumer Act, which agency sets standards for agricultural products?
e: Art. 6 assigns agricultural products to DA.
DOH covers food, drugs, cosmetics and devices.

s: The Consumer Act's state policy aims to protect consumers' interests and:
o: Fix the price of every product
Set standards of conduct for business and industry

s: A buyer chooses fair-trade products to support poor farmers. Which consumer responsibility is this?
o: Assertiveness in getting a fair deal
Critical awareness of price and quality
e: Awareness of the effect of consumption on others, especially the disadvantaged, is social concern.

s: The Consumer Act also requires a consumer education program for:
Under Art. 159, departments must set up complaint procedures that are:
e: The law requires simple, accessible procedures.

s: A store displays canned goods with no price tag, label or marking. Under Art. 81 this is:
o: Allowed if the cashier knows the price
Not allowed; products for retail need a displayed price
e: Art. 81 requires a price tag, label or marking.

s: An imported jar of jam has no country of manufacture on its label. Which rule is broken?
e: The missing item is the country.
Country of manufacture is required for imports.

s: A rice cooker's warranty card does not say who the warrantor is or how long the coverage lasts. Which rule does this break?
o: Art. 68(a), requiring clear terms of express warranties
e: The warranty must state the warrantor and period.

s: A person in Cebu buys shoes from an online shop that targets Philippine buyers. Is the transaction covered by RA 11967?
o: No; online shoes are online media content
Yes; it is a B2C internet transaction targeting the Philippine market
No; only government purchases are covered
No; only purchases above ₱1 million are covered

s: A family earns ₱25,000 a month. Under the 50-30-20 guide, how much is for needs?
e: That is 20%, for savings and debt.

s: Which of the following is a VARIABLE expense?
e: The source lists internet as fixed.

e: Divide the bill by the months it covers: 900 ÷ 3.

s: Which of the following is a common competency in Housekeeping NC II?
e: This is among the listed units.

s: How many classes of nutrients are there?
e: Five leaves out one class; water is often forgotten.
Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, water, vitamins and minerals.
Four leaves out two classes, such as water and minerals.
Fiber is not counted as a separate class in our source.

s: Which of the following is NOT a macronutrient?
e: Vitamins are micronutrients, needed in small amounts.

s: How many essential minerals and vitamins does our source list as micronutrients?
e: Micronutrients are the 16 essential minerals and 13 vitamins.

s: A snack has 10 g carbohydrate, 5 g protein and 4 g fat. About how many kilocalories does it provide?
e: This counts fat at 4 kcal/g instead of 9.
This counts every gram at 9 kcal.

s: According to our nutrition source, what is protein's MOST important job?
o: Building body structures and running chemical reactions
Supplying most of the body's daily energy needs for work and exercise
e: Proteins build bones, muscles and skin and run most chemical reactions; energy is not their main job.
The source says energy is not protein's most important job.
Iron, a mineral, helps red blood cells carry oxygen.
Insulation is a role of lipids.

s: Which nutrient class forms cell membranes, protects organs and helps regulate body temperature?
e: Minerals are micronutrients with other roles.
Lipids form membranes, protect organs and insulate the body.

s: Why is a daily source of vitamin C needed?
o: It is stored in body fat for years, so a large dose lasts a long time
It is not stored in significant amounts; excess is excreted
It is a mineral used up in sweat
It is made in the skin from sunlight
e: That describes fat-soluble vitamins more closely.
The source says vitamin C is not stored much and higher intake means more is excreted.
Vitamin C is a vitamin, not a mineral.

s: Which of the following is NOT a B vitamin?
e: Vitamin K is fat-soluble, not a B vitamin.

s: A sailor on a long voyage without fresh fruit develops bleeding gums and slow-healing wounds. Which nutrient is lacking?
e: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness.
Bleeding gums and poor healing are signs of scurvy, from lack of vitamin C, which is needed for collagen.

s: Vitamin C is essential for making which structural protein?
e: Keratin is the protein in hair and wool, not linked here.
The source links vitamin C to collagen synthesis, which is why scurvy affects gums and skin.
Albumin is linked to edema in kwashiorkor.

s: In adults, vitamin D deficiency causes which condition?
e: Vitamin D deficiency gives rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

s: In a community whose staple is polished white rice, a nurse sees leg pain, swelling and signs of heart failure. Which deficiency fits?
e: Beriberi is common where the staple is milled white rice, because milling removes the bran.

s: Why is beriberi common where milled white rice is the main food?
o: White rice contains a vitamin C blocker
Rice is too high in iodine
e: The source says milling removes the bran.
The source gives no such cause.

s: Which set lists the "four D's" of pellagra given in our source?
o: Diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia and sometimes death
Diarrhea, diabetes, dehydration, dementia and depression
e: These are not the four D's.
Niacin deficiency leads to diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia and sometimes death.
These are not the four D's.
Diabetes and dehydration are not part of the list.

s: Dry eyes with Bitot's spots that can progress to corneal ulcers and blindness describe:
o: Scurvy from a long-term lack of vitamin C in the diet
Xerophthalmia from severe vitamin A deficiency
e: Scurvy affects gums, skin and joints.
Severe vitamin A deficiency causes xerophthalmia.

s: Low iron intake causes anemia mainly because it:
o: Reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of red blood cells
Causes edema because the blood cannot hold enough water and albumin
e: That is goiter, from iodine deficiency.
The source explains anemia this way.

s: Iodine is essential for making which hormone?
e: Thyroid hormone affects growth, but iodine is used for thyroid hormone.
Iodine is needed to make thyroid hormone, which regulates basal metabolism, growth and development.
Adrenaline is not made from iodine.
Insulin is not made from iodine.

s: Why does a child with kwashiorkor show swelling (edema)?
o: Lack of vitamin C weakens vessels
Too much salt in the diet makes the body hold water in every tissue
Too little protein means too little albumin to hold water in the blood vessels
e: The source does not give salt as the cause.
The source explains edema through low albumin.

s: A recently weaned toddler fed mostly thin rice porridge has a pot belly, swollen feet and thinning, light-colored hair. The most likely condition is:
e: Recently weaned children on low-protein porridge with edema and light, thin hair fit kwashiorkor.
Marasmus shows extreme thinness without edema.

s: The word "marasmus" comes from Greek and means:
e: "Rejected one" is the meaning of kwashiorkor (from Ghana).
The source says marasmus is Greek for starvation.

s: The name "kwashiorkor" comes from a language of which country?
e: The source says the name comes from a language in Ghana, meaning "rejected one".
Not the source of the name.
Not the source of the name.

s: Which list gives the four steps of safe food handling?
e: These are not the four named steps.
These are the four steps in the source.
These are not the four named steps.

s: Within how many hours should leftovers be refrigerated?
o: Only after they cool completely overnight
e: The Chill step says refrigerate leftovers within two hours.
Twelve hours is far too long.
Waiting overnight leaves food in unsafe temperatures.

s: At what temperature or colder should a refrigerator be kept?
Where in the refrigerator should raw meat be stored?
e: The door is the warmest part.
Juices could drip onto foods below.
Storing raw meat at the bottom keeps its juices from dripping onto other foods.

s: Why should eggs be kept on a shelf rather than in the refrigerator door?
o: The door is the warmest part of the refrigerator
Light from the door bulb damages the shells
e: Cleanliness is not the reason given.
The source says the door is warmest.
That is not the reason given.

s: Hot food that is being held for serving should be kept above about:
e: Hot food should be kept above 140 °F.
That is in the danger range.
Food need not be kept boiling.

s: A foodborne illness caused by toxins (for example, produced by molds) rather than by live microbes is called:
e: Foodborne illnesses are infections (microbes) or intoxications (toxins).
Allergies are immune reactions, not this category.
Infections are caused by the microbes themselves.

s: Salmonellosis symptoms usually appear within:
e: The source gives fever, diarrhea and cramps within 12–72 hours.

s: Salmonella is found mainly in the intestines of:
o: Molds, yeasts and other fungi on bread
e: It is not limited to fish.
Those are fungi, not hosts of Salmonella.
The source says Salmonella lives in these animals' intestines.
Salmonella is linked to animal sources.

s: Molds grow best on food kept in which conditions?
e: Cold, dry conditions slow mold growth.
Molds are fungi that grow in warm, humid or damp conditions.

s: When an egg white turns from clear to white while cooking, what is happening to its proteins?
e: Cooking denatures proteins and changes their functional qualities.

s: Which of the following is a MODERN rather than traditional preservation method in our source?
e: Modern methods include drying, vacuum packing, pasteurization, freezing and refrigeration.

s: Besides preventing foodborne illness, food preservation also protects:
o: Only the calorie count and the weight of the food
Flavor, color, moisture and nutritive value
e: Price is not the listed benefit.
Weight is not the listed benefit.

s: Under the Food Fortification Act, "fortification" means adding nutrients to processed foods at levels:
e: The law defines the term; the choice is not free.
RA 8976 Sec. 3 defines fortification this way.

s: A carinderia owner asks what salt the ASIN law lets her offer customers. What is the answer?
e: RA 8172 requires food outlets and restaurants to make only iodized salt available.
The law regulates salt; it does not ban it.
The law does not require rock salt.

s: The Food Safety Act of 2013 (RA 10611) aims to protect the public from:
o: Imported foods of all kinds, which the Act bans from local markets
Food-borne and water-borne illness and unsafe or misbranded food
e: Price control is not its aim.
Its aim is food safety broadly.

s: Poaching differs from boiling and simmering mainly because it uses:
o: Dry oven air at a high, steady temperature
e: Poaching uses a gentler, lower temperature than simmering or boiling.

s: In blanching, plunging vegetables into iced water right after boiling is called:
e: The cold plunge that stops cooking is known as shocking or refreshing.
Searing is browning at high heat.
Basting is spooning liquid over food.

s: The word "sauté" comes from French and refers to:
o: Marinating the food overnight before cooking it
Jumping or tossing the food in the pan
e: Sauté means "jumped", from tossing while cooking.

s: A cook browns beef chunks in a hot pan, then adds a little broth, covers the pot and cooks it slowly. Which method is this, and why is it NOT poaching?
o: Sautéing, because the beef was browned
Braising, because it starts with dry-heat browning before covered simmering
Steaming, because the pot is covered and the liquid makes steam around the beef
e: Poaching does not begin with browning.
Sautéing is quick cooking in fat only.
Braising combines dry and wet heat; poaching only uses gentle liquid heat.
Steaming cooks with steam, not in liquid after browning.

s: Pan-frying differs from deep-frying because in pan-frying the food is:
e: Deep-frying submerges food in hot fat; shallow (pan) frying does not.

s: A cook soaks pork in vinegar, soy sauce and garlic for an hour before grilling. This step is called:
e: Creaming is beating fat with sugar.
Blanching is brief boiling then shocking.
Braising is a cooking method, not a soak.
Soaking food in a seasoned, often acidic liquid before cooking is marinating.

s: Why are vegetables often diced into uniform cubes?
o: To make them float in oil
e: Dicing is not for removing vitamins.

s: Under PD 856, utensils are washed in warm water at what temperature?
e: 77 °C is for hot-water sanitizing, not washing.
Boiling is not the washing temperature.

s: For hot-water sanitizing under PD 856, utensils are immersed for at least 30 seconds in water at:
o: 82 °C in a hot-air cabinet for only 20 seconds
e: That is below the required temperature.
Sec. 25 sets at least 30 seconds at 77 °C.
That is the hot-air cabinet option.

s: If chlorine is used to sanitize utensils, PD 856 calls for immersion for at least:
o: 1 minute in a lukewarm 50 ppm chlorine solution
30 minutes in a 500 ppm chlorine solution at boiling point
e: Water alone is not a chlorine treatment.

s: Which order of steps follows PD 856 for washing utensils?
o: Scrape and pre-rinse, wash in warm detergent water, sanitize, drain-dry
Sanitize, scrape and pre-rinse, wash in cold water, towel-dry
e: Scraping and washing come before sanitizing; drying cloths are not used.

s: After sanitizing, a canteen worker wipes each plate dry with a cloth. What does PD 856 say?
o: Any cloth is fine if it is new
Utensils should drain-dry on racks without drying cloths
Plates must be dried with paper only
Cloth drying is required so that no chlorine taste remains on plates
e: The law says no drying cloths.
The law says drain-dry or air-dry.
The law says no drying cloths.

s: Under PD 856, which materials must NOT be used in food equipment?
o: Food-grade plastic containers with tight-fitting lids
e: This is not banned in the law's text.

s: Under PD 856, perishable foods are kept at or below what temperature, except during preparation or serving?
e: The rule is at or below 7 °C.

s: PD 856 recommends storing meat and fish at:
e: That is for fruits and vegetables.
That is for milk and milk products.
Sec. 29(c) gives 0–3 °C for meat and fish.

s: Under PD 856, fruits and vegetables are best stored at:
e: That is for meat and fish.

s: What does PD 856 recommend for storing dry, non-perishable foods?
o: Any container at room temperature, as long as it is labeled
The same shelf as cleaning chemicals
Metal containers with tight covers, at about 10–15 °C
e: Designated shelves and covered containers are required.
That is unsafe and not the rule.

s: Under PD 856, refrigerators used for food must have:
o: Thermometers and enough shelving for ventilation
A lock on every shelf and a glass door for display

s: How should cups and glasses be stored under PD 856?
o: Upright on the bottom shelf of the open cabinet below the work top
Inverted, in a clean, dry place protected from vermin
e: Bottom shelves below the work top are not allowed.
They are stored in a clean, dry place.
Sec. 27 says cups, bowls and glasses are inverted.

s: A server picks up ice for a drink with bare fingers. Under PD 856 this is:
o: Not allowed; hand contact with food must be avoided
Allowed if the server's hands look clean and dry
e: Sec. 30(a) says fingers are not used for butter, ice and similar items.
Consent does not change the rule.

s: Under PD 856, how should sugar be served in a food establishment?
o: In open bowls shared by all tables, refilled from a sack
In covered dispensers or single-service packets
Only on request, from the kitchen floor
e: Open bowls are not the rule.

s: Where do soiled linens go under PD 856?
o: On the dining chairs until closing
e: Clean and soiled linens are separated.
Sec. 30(d) requires a closed, marked bin.

s: Under PD 856, between uses, ice cream dippers and scoops are kept:
o: In running water or water at 77 °C, or washed and dried after each use
In a dry cup on the counter
In a drawer with the cleaning cloths, dried by hand each morning
e: That is not an option given.
That is not an option given.
That is not an option given.

s: In which service style is food plated in the kitchen and brought to each guest?
e: Guests serve themselves at a buffet.
That is not one of the three styles listed.

s: Which order follows the F&B Services NC II sequence of service?
o: Present the bill, greet, seat, take orders
Greet, seat, take beverage orders, present menu, take food orders
Serve food, present menu, greet, seat
Take food orders, greet, seat, present menu, take beverage orders
e: This is the start of the listed sequence.
The menu is presented before food is served.

s: What is the purpose of the "3-minute check"?
o: To time how fast the kitchen cooks each order for the manager
To count the cutlery before service
To confirm guest satisfaction soon after serving
e: The check confirms satisfaction and replenishes items.

s: In the sequence of service, crumbing the table comes:
o: After serving food, before coffee or tea
After presenting the bill and collecting payment
e: The sequence is serve food, crumb, then coffee/tea, then the bill.

s: Which of the following is NOT part of closing down the dining area in the TR?
o: Handling food scraps according to hygiene rules
e: The TR says turn off electrical equipment.

s: When preparing the dining area, what does the TR say about condiment bottles?
o: Fill them only after guests arrive
e: That is not in the TR.
The TR lists wiping necks and tops of condiment bottles.
That is not in the TR.

s: A bakery learns that a batch of bread may be contaminated and some loaves were already sold. Under RA 10611, what must it do?
o: Lower the price to sell it faster
Wait for a customer complaint before removing any bread from the shelves
Keep selling and hope no one gets sick
Withdraw the bread, inform authorities and consumers, and recall it
e: The duty to act is immediate.
Sec. 14 requires withdrawal, notice and recall.

s: Under the Food Safety Act, who is responsible for food safety in school canteens?
e: Sec. 15 assigns food businesses such as school canteens to LGUs.
DOH covers processed and prepackaged foods.

s: Under RA 10611, which agency covers food safety in primary production (farms)?
e: Sec. 15 assigns primary production to the DA.
LGUs cover food businesses like markets and canteens.

s: Under RA 11037, which agency runs the school-based feeding program for undernourished public school children?
o: Department of Health (DOH) through rural health units
e: DOH is not named as the operator here.
DSWD runs supplemental feeding in day care centers.
DepEd runs the program from kindergarten to Grade 6.

s: RA 11037 feeding programs give at least one fortified meal for not less than how many days a year?
e: The law says not less than 120.

s: Under RA 11037, a fortified meal supplies at least what share of the daily requirement?
e: Sec. 3(a) says at least one-third, based on the PDRI.

s: The DSWD supplemental feeding under RA 11037 covers children aged:
e: The law does not cover this group here.
The law names ages 3 to 5 in day care.

s: Which is NOT a component of the feeding program under RA 11037?
e: The components include milk feeding, supplements, deworming, Gulayan sa Paaralan, WASH and nutrition education.

s: HACCP addresses which kinds of food hazards?
o: Only those found after the food is served
e: Chemical and physical hazards are included.

s: By 1997, how many HACCP principles had become the standard?
A canteen stores milk at 12 °C. Under PD 856's recommended range, what is wrong?
o: Nothing; 12 °C is the milk range in PD 856
Milk must always be frozen solid
It is too warm; milk should be kept at 5–7 °C
It is too cold; milk should be kept at 20 °C

s: Under PD 856, food-contact surfaces of equipment must be:
o: Impervious, corrosion-resistant, non-toxic, easy to clean and durable
Porous so that they absorb cleaning water

s: Single-service items such as paper cups should be:
o: Stored loose on the floor near the sink
Stored in sanitary cartons and handled without touching food-contact surfaces
Handled by the rim to show cleanliness
Reused after rinsing with cold water

s: In Russian service, food is served from:
e: That is not a listed style.

s: Under RA 11037, the cycle menus are standardized by:
o: The National Nutrition Council and FNRI

s: Under RA 11037, the school gardens program is called:
e: The law names Gulayan sa Paaralan.

s: Under the Family Code, what is the minimum age at which a person may contract marriage?
e: 21 matters only for the parental-consent rule; it is not the minimum age.
Art. 5 sets the minimum marrying age at 18.
Below 18 the marriage is void even with parental consent (Art. 35).
25 is not the Family Code's minimum age.

s: Which of the following is an ESSENTIAL (not formal) requisite of marriage under the Family Code?
o: A ceremony with two adult witnesses
Consent freely given before the solemnizing officer
e: The ceremony is a formal requisite (Art. 3).
The license is a formal requisite (Art. 3).
Art. 2 lists legal capacity and freely given consent as the essential requisites.
Officer's authority is a formal requisite (Art. 3).

s: Which of the following is a FORMAL requisite of marriage under the Family Code?
o: Approval of both sets of parents
A valid marriage license, unless exempt
e: Parental approval is not a general requisite.
Legal capacity is an essential requisite (Art. 2).
Art. 3 lists the officer's authority, a valid license and the ceremony as formal requisites.

s: How many witnesses of legal age must be present at the marriage ceremony under the Family Code?
o: None, if a license was issued
e: Art. 3 requires the declaration before at least two witnesses of legal age.
The Code says at least two, not three.
One witness is not enough under Art. 3.
The license does not remove the witness requirement.

s: The Family Code defines marriage as which of the following?
o: A civil partnership that may be ended by mutual agreement
A special contract of permanent union between a man and a woman
A temporary contract renewed every ten years
A religious sacrament recognized only by the Church
e: The Code calls it a permanent union, not a dissolvable partnership.
Art. 1 uses these words and calls marriage the foundation of the family.
The Code treats it as a special contract under law.

s: Ana, 17, marries with her parents' written consent. What is the status of the marriage?
o: Void, because a party is below 18
e: A void marriage is not cured by reaching 18.
Art. 35 makes marriages of persons below 18 void even with parental consent.
Parental consent cannot cure being below 18.
The voidable rule covers ages 18 to below 21 without consent.

s: Ben, 19, marries without his parents' consent and leaves his wife before turning 21. What is the status of the marriage?
o: Valid only if a church wedding was held
e: The type of ceremony does not decide this.
Lack of parental consent at 18–20 gives a voidable, not void, marriage.
Art. 45 makes a marriage of a party aged 18 to below 21 without parental consent voidable.
Art. 45 allows annulment in this case.

s: A party aged 20 married without parental consent, then freely lived with the spouse as husband and wife after turning 21. What follows?
o: The ground for annulment is lost by the free cohabitation
The parents may still annul it at any time
e: Art. 45 excepts cases where the party freely cohabited after reaching 21.
Free cohabitation after 21 removes this ground.
Free cohabitation after 21 cures the defect; it does not make it void.
The Code does not require a new ceremony.

s: Under the Family Code, a marriage in which one party was psychologically incapacitated to comply with essential marital obligations is:
o: Valid if the couple has children
e: Having children does not change Art. 36.
Psychological incapacity falls under Art. 36 (void), not Art. 45.
Civil status is governed by the Family Code.
Art. 36 makes such a marriage void, even if the incapacity shows only after the wedding.

s: Which of the following marriages is NOT void under Art. 35 of the Family Code?
o: One solemnized without a license, not exempt
One where a 19-year-old married without parental consent
e: Below 18 is void even with consent.
Bigamous and polygamous marriages are void.
Lack of a license (unless exempt) makes it void.
That case is voidable under Art. 45, not void.

s: What is the effect of the absence of any essential or formal requisite of marriage, as a general rule?
o: The marriage becomes a legal separation
The marriage is voidable for five years
The marriage is void from the beginning
The marriage is valid but the officer is fined
e: Legal separation is a different remedy.
Absence of a requisite gives a void marriage.
Art. 4 says absence of any requisite makes it void ab initio (subject to Art. 35(2)).
The Code treats absence as voiding the marriage.

s: Under the Family Code, who exercises parental authority over the common children of a married couple?
o: The father and the mother jointly
e: Grandparents exercise substitute authority only in specific cases.
Art. 211 gives parental authority to both parents jointly.
Authority is joint; the father's view prevails only when they disagree.

s: A couple disagrees about which school their son should attend, and no court order exists. Under Art. 211, whose decision prevails?
o: The father's, unless a court orders otherwise
The child's, if aged 12 or above
e: Art. 211 says the father's decision prevails in case of disagreement, unless a court orders otherwise.
Art. 211 does not give the child the deciding vote.
The school has no authority to decide.
The Code gives the father's decision priority here.

s: A 12-year-old living with his parents breaks a neighbor's window. Who is civilly liable for the damage?
o: His parents, subject to the defenses allowed by law
No one, because he is a minor
Only the child, from his future earnings
e: Art. 221 makes parents civilly liable for damage by unemancipated children living with them.
Minority shifts civil liability to the parents.
Art. 221 places liability on the parents.
The barangay is not liable under Art. 221.

s: Under RA 7610, a "child" generally refers to a person:
e: RA 7610 Sec. 3(a) defines children as persons below 18, or older but unable to protect themselves.

s: The Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act (RA 10354) defines adolescents as young people aged:
e: The RH Law's range is 10 to 19.
The RH Law's range is 10 to 19.
RA 10354 Sec. 4(b) defines adolescents as ages 10 to 19.
The RH Law's range is 10 to 19.

s: Under RA 9262, which of the following is a form of violence against women and their children?
o: A teacher's low grade given fairly
Economic abuse by a former husband
A stranger's theft of a woman's phone
e: A fair grade is not abuse.
RA 9262 covers physical, sexual, psychological harm and economic abuse by a husband, former husband or partner.
RA 9262 concerns persons in an intimate or family relationship.
That is a civil matter, not VAWC.

s: The Early Years Act treats which age range as the first crucial stage of educational development?
e: The Early Years Act covers ages 0 to 8.

s: The family a person is born into is called the family of:
e: The family of procreation is formed through marriage.
The family of orientation is the one you are born into.
Adoption is a way of forming a family, not this term.
Affinity refers to relatives by marriage, not this definition.

s: A married couple and the children they raise together form, for the parents, their family of:

Two dots, the same as denim

e: These are color groupings, not the three properties.

s: A color scheme that uses tints and shades of a single hue is:
e: Analogous uses neighbors on the wheel.
Monochromatic uses one hue's tints and shades.
Triadic uses three evenly spaced hues.

e: Analogous colors are side by side.

s: A triadic color scheme uses:

e: Triadic means three evenly spaced hues.

A base color plus the two colors beside its complement
Two pairs of complements forming a rectangle
Tints of one color split by white

s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a basic/block pattern in the Dressmaking TR?

s: On a pattern, notches mark:

Only the brand of the pattern
Seam allowances, centerlines, zipper placement and matching points

s: On US care labels, washing temperature is shown by:

s: The color property that refers to brightness or dullness (chroma) is:

s: A tracing wheel is also known as a:

e: That is not in our source.

A DOLE inspector assigned to the region

s: Under RA 11058, the fine for willful non-compliance is up to:

Only the workers who were injured

Alone and kept secret from workers
In consultation with workers, then submitted to DOLE

Sec. 12 requires consultation and submission to DOLE.

s: Which is NOT listed as part of a workplace safety and health program under RA 11058?

s: Under RA 11058, what must welfare facilities include where applicable?

Air-conditioned offices for all workers and visitors

A health certificate for the building from the city engineer
A permit from the Department of Education

A health certificate from the local health authority
A sanitary permit in their own name

Chosen only by their price at the market
Estimated by eye to save time during busy hours
Selected, measured and weighed according to the recipe
